page: Vultr vcg-a16-2c-8g-2vram is a Cloud GPU server instance configured with an Intel x86_64 processor offering 2 dedicated vCPUs from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and features 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, equating to 4.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the instance includes a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPU with a 0.125 allocation, providing 2 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mix of average single-core capabilities and weaker multi-core and memory throughput. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1420.0 and a multi-core score of 2578.0. Stress-ng single-core CPU performance reached 1781.78, while multi-core performance was measured at 3465.56. Memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with large block read-only speeds at 27.11 GB/sec and write speeds at 19.81 GB/sec. However, the hardware demonstrates strong efficiency in specific tasks, notably achieving a top-tier prompt processing speed of 7078.28 tokens/sec for a small 135M LLM model, alongside an average text generation speed of 233.47 tokens/sec.

This instance represents an entry-level GPU-accelerated tier, trading raw multi-core compute and memory bandwidth for cost-efficient access to hardware acceleration. While database operations and ray tracing benchmarks are poor, the server is well-suited for lightweight GPU-assisted workloads, small-scale LLM inference prompt processing, basic image processing, and general-purpose tasks that benefit from a dedicated Intel CPU and fractional NVIDIA Ampere resources.
